vivac_rule.verbatim: establecer las regulaciones oportunas. 9.2.1.3. La pernocta 9.2.1.3.1. Vivac y acampada nocturna. La actividad del vivac o acampada nocturna queda prohibida en el sector Ordesa, con la excepción, hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2023, de un cupo de 90 personas que se establece para la Zona de Uso Moderado de Góriz en los casos de aforo completo del refugio. A partir de esa fecha dicho cupo quedará reducido a 50 personas. En todo caso, la pernocta no excederá de tres noches. En el resto de sectores del Parque Nacional esta actividad queda restringida a los terrenos por encima de las siguientes cotas de altitud, estableciendo que la pernocta en un mismo sector no excederá de tres noches: · Añisclo: 1.650 m. findings: Mapa 88 exists, is named by the rule text itself (Vease Anexo 11.5 Cartografia. Mapa 88), and shows the four 'Zonas de Vivac' polygons (Ordesa/Añisclo/Escuaín/Pineta) defined by altitude quotas (2.500/1.650/1.800/2.550 m) with total area 7.511,17 ha.

Mapa 88 does NOT draw a Sector Ordesa boundary: the polygons it delimits are altitude bands (vivac areas), not the sector. The sector is defined elsewhere in the text by the Arazas hydrographic basin, a watershed that no annex page draws as a line.

STALENESS / CONFLICT: Mapa 88 is dated 2013 and its legend reads 'Ordesa: cota 2.500 metros' (i.e. vivac permitted above 2.500 m in Ordesa), while the operative 2022 text PROHIBITS vivac in the whole Sector Ordesa except the Góriz quota. The annex map is therefore not the current expression of the rule and must not be used as its operative geometry.

GORIZ legal link PROVEN: PRUG text names 'Zona de acampada de alta montaña adyacente al refugio de Góriz' with explicit reference 'Anexo 11.5 Cartografía. Mapa 29' -> the legal chain for that polygon is now demonstrable (was grade-B candidate in the WFS discovery).

The annex carries an orphaned OCG registry (2.231 entries; 174 unique layer names) but no page paints a layer named sector/vivac/acampada: the geometry is flattened into generic layers, so even a hypothetical conversion could not tag-separate it reliably.
derivation_path_if_reopened: sector boundary = watershed of Rio Arazas per PRUG 9.2.1; a reproducible derivation would need an explicit protocol (pour points, official DEM MDT02 already identified in the WFS phase, hydrography source, documented parameters) plus independent human review; this is OUR derived geometry from official normative cartography, never 'official vector geometry'.

policy.mapa_88_as_operative_geometry: FORBIDDEN (2013 vintage, contradicts 2022 text for Ordesa)
